The '''2026 Varsity Cup''' was the 19th season of the [[Varsity Rugby#Varsity Cup|Varsity Cup]], the premier competition in the annual [[Varsity Rugby]] series in South Africa for men's [[rugby union]]. The tournament took place between eight university teams and played between 16 February and 13 April 2026.<ref name="VC2026">{{Cite web |title=Varsity Cup 2026 Fixtures & Results |url=https://www.varsitycup.co.za/varsity-cup-fixtures-logs |website=Varsity Cup |access-date=16 February 2026}}</ref> {{Rut|UP Tuks}} were crowned champions, securing a record sixth [[Varsity Cup]] title, the most by any team in the competition's history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tuks claim record-breaking title |url= https://www.sarugbymag.co.za/tuks-claim-record-breaking-title/#:~:text=Tuks%20dominated%20the%20NWU%20Eagles,tight%20exchanges%20among%20the%20forwards. |website=SA Rugby May |access-date=13 April 2026}}</ref>

This competition forms part of the broader Varsity Rugby programme administered by Varsity Sport, which aims to promote university rugby and provide a pathway for emerging talent into professional rugby structures.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Varsity Rugby |url=https://www.varsitycup.co.za/about/ |website=Varsity Cup |access-date=16 February 2026}}</ref> Matches were broadcast nationally on [[SuperSport (South African broadcaster)|SuperSport]].

The {{Rut|UCT Ikey Tigers}} entered the 2026 season as the former winners of the Varsity Cup Trophy after beating Maties in the 2025 final.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ikey Tigers Pounce into the Varsity Cup Season|url=https://varsitynewspaper.substack.com/p/ikey-tigers-pounce-into-the-varsity |website=Varsity Newspaper|access-date=9 March 2026}}</ref> The 2026 edition was staged under the campaign theme "Who's NXT?", highlighting Varsity Cup's role as a launchpad for future professional and international players and introducing the new Tap-or-Kick post-try power play law to further encourage attacking rugby.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FNB Varsity Cup and Shield 2026 to Showcase Rugby's Future Talent |url=https://www.varsitycup.co.za/news/fnb-varsity-cup-and-shield-2026-to-showcase-rugby-s-future-talent |website=Varsity Cup |access-date=16 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Varsity Cup rule tweaks favour attack in 2026 |url=https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-02-16-varsity-cup-rule-tweaks-favour-attack-in-2026/ |website=Daily maverick|access-date=9 March 2026}}</ref> Matches were broadcast nationally on [[SuperSport (South African broadcaster)|SuperSport]].

==Competition rules and information==

Eight university teams participated in the 2026 Varsity Cup. During the pool stage, each team played the other seven sides once, either home or away.<ref name="VC2026" />

Teams were awarded:
* four points for a win
* two points for a draw
* one bonus point for scoring four or more tries in a match
* one bonus point for losing by seven points or fewer

Teams were ranked primarily by log points, and then by points difference (points scored minus points conceded).<ref name="VC2026" />

The top four teams at the conclusion of the pool stage advanced to the [[#Semifinals|semi-finals]]. The two highest-ranked teams hosted the semi-finals, and the highest-ranked remaining finalist hosted the [[#Final|final]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Varsity Cup Competition Rules |url=https://www.varsitycup.co.za/rules/ |website=Varsity Cup |access-date=16 February 2026}}</ref>

===Promotion and relegation===
At the end of the Varsity Cup season, a promotion–relegation system determined the movement between the Varsity Cup and the Varsity Shield. The team that finished last in the [[Varsity Cup]] standings is automatically relegated to the [[Varsity Shield]] for the following season.

The winner of the [[Varsity Shield]] is automatically promoted to the [[Varsity Cup]]. In addition, the second-last placed [[Varsity Cup]] which was  [[Varsity College (South Africa)|Emeris]]  played a promotion–relegation playoff match against the [[Varsity Shield]] runner-up which was {{Rut|WSU All Blacks}}, with the winner earning a place in next season's Varsity Cup. [[Varsity College (South Africa)|Emeris]] came out on top and retained their place in the Varsity Cup for 2027.

{{rugbybox
